title: Methodology for Biomimetic Chemical Neuromodulation of Rat Retinas with the Neurotransmitter Glutamate In Vitro
protocol: Procure a 24 - 32 day old wild-type Long Evans Hooded rat of either sex.
Raise the rat with a standard 12 h day/night rhythm.
Dark adapt the rat by placing it in a completely dark room for 1 hour prior to beginning the experiment.
Cross the transgenic albino homozygous S334ter-3 rat line (either sex) with a pigmented wild-type Long-Evans rat to produce heterozygous offspring.
Raise the heterozygous offspring with a standard 12 h day/night rhythm and use rats of either sex for experiments at ages corresponding to different stages of photoreceptor degeneration.
Dark adapt the rat by placing it in a completely dark room for 1 hour prior to beginning the experiment.
Measure out 900 mL of de-ionized water and place in a 1 L container.
Perfuse the water with 100% CO2 using a bubbling mechanism.
Add 8.8 g of powdered Ames' medium to the water in the 1 L container.
Rinse the Ames' medium container with a few mL of de-ionized water and add to the 1 L container.
Add 25.3 mL of sodium bicarbonate solution (7.5% w/v) to the 1 L container.
Add additional water to bring the solution to a final volume of 1 L.
Continue perfusing the water with CO2 for approximately 5 min.
Stop CO2 perfusion and begin perfusing the solution with a medical-grade gas mixture of 95% O2 and 5% CO2 for at least 30 min or until the pH stabilizes at 7.4.
Keep Ames medium at room temperature (~21 °C) throughout the experiment.
Clean bottom and top perfusion tubes with 70% ethanol.
Wash both perfusion lines three times with de-ionized water.
Fill the bottom line with de-ionized water.
Fill the top line with air.
Close both lines using a solenoid valve system.
Attach main perfusion tube to luer connection of Ames medium container.
Open the top perfusion valve until solution exits from the top perfusion outlet.
Turn off the top perfusion valve.
Open the bottom perfusion outlet until all bubbles exit through the bottom outlet.
Attach an empty suction vessel to the main suction line.
Turn on the suction source.
Ensure that both the top and bottom suction inlets are open and working.
Cover computer displays with red filter screens.
Euthanize animal via carbon dioxide asphyxiation followed by cervical dislocation according to IACUC protocols.
Enucleate both eyes using a jeweler's #5 forceps.
Place enucleated eyes in a 60 mm diameter petri dish with approximately 3 - 4 mL of fresh, oxygenated Ames medium solution.
Make a small incision in the corneal face using a scalpel or a pair of sharp scissors.
Cut from this small incision to the edge of the cornea then extend the cut in a circumferential section around the entire edge of the cornea.
Remove the detached cornea along with the lens, aqueous and vitreous humors.
Hold the eyecup gently with one pair of forceps.
Make two small incisions on opposite sides of the eyecup.
Use two pairs of forceps to gently pull apart the eyecup at each of the incisions and separate the retina from the sclera.
Slowly lift the entire retina from the sclera and eyecup.
Cut the optic nerve if it is still attached.
Make longitudinal cuts in the retina to obtain half or quarter sections using scissors.
Gently spread one retinal section onto a nylon mesh with the ganglion cells facing away from the mesh.
Place the mesh and retina onto a perforated multielectrode array (pMEA) with ganglion cells in contact with the pMEA surface.
Gently place a weighted slice grid on top of the mesh to hold the retina in place.
Under dim red illumination, place pMEA in MEA amplifier.
Close amplifier latches.
Etch two 'X'-shaped marks spaced approximately 5 mm apart on the pMEA chamber ring if not already present.
Position the top perfusion outlet inside the pMEA chamber.
Turn on the top perfusion valve to achieve a perfusion rate of approximately 3 mL per minute.
Position the top suction inlet at the desired perfusate level (~5 mm deep).
Ensure the top suction inlet is working properly.
Open the data acquisition software on the data acquisition computer and click the 'play' button to start receiving data.
Ensure all pMEA channels are noise-free and recording neural signals.
Reposition the pMEA within the amplifier if necessary to obtain better contact between the amplifier pins and the pMEA contacts.
Ensure that the bottom perfusion line is clear of any air bubbles.
Turn on the bottom perfusion valve once the bottom perfusion line is bubble-free.
Open imaging software and turn on the high-speed camera attached to the inverted optical microscope (10X magnification with N.A. of 0.45).
Cover the inverted microscope illuminator with a red filter sheet to emit only red light.
Set the illuminator to a low light level to avoid photobleaching the retina.
Observe the bottom surface of the pMEA for evidence that solution is flowing through the bottom perfusion plate.
Slowly ramp up the bottom suction by manually turning the vacuum pressure knob on the vacuum waste kit while observing the retina through the inverted microscope.
Cease increasing the suction once an observable suction force acts on the retina.
Take the weighted slice grid off the retina using forceps.
Gently remove the nylon mesh by peeling one corner carefully from the retina.
Keep perfusion running for approximately 30 min to allow the retina to stabilize from surgical trauma.
Prepare glutamate solution by mixing stock glutamate solution with oxygenated Ames medium solution to obtain a 0.5 mL sample at a working concentration of 1 mM glutamate.

Insert a pre-pulled 10 µm-diameter micropipette or the stainless steel rod connected to the multiport microfluidic device into a standard pipette holder containing a 50 µm-diameter silver/silver chloride wire electrode.
Interface the pipette holder with the patch-clamp headstage and connect the pressure port luer connection of the pipette holder to channel 1 of the pressure injection system.
Manually turn on the pressure injection system and turn on channel 1 (or channels 1 - 8, as applicable).
Ensure that the system is vented to atmosphere and set the injection pressure to 0.1 psi.
Calibrate the micromanipulator by pressing the 'Calibrate' button on the manipulator controller.
Position the micropipette tip or the bottom of the device approximately 30 mm above the MEA amplifier.
Fill a small petri dish with glutamate solution (1 mM glutamate in standard Ames medium).
Lower micropipette tip into the glutamate solution.
Press the 'Fill' button on the pressure injection system until there is approximately 20 mm of solution visible in the glass micropipette.
Turn channel 1 of the pressure injector off if using the multiport device.
Repeat the protocol for channels 2 to 8 if using the multiport device.
Lift the micropipette tip or device out of the solution and remove the petri dish.
Position the micromanipulator above the pMEA chamber.
Align the micropipette tip with the reference marks etched into the pMEA chamber ring.
Store the manipulator positions into the control software using the 'Store Reference A' and 'Store Reference B' buttons.
Select a target pMEA electrode with robust spontaneous activity.
Click the 'Move to Channel' button to align the glass micropipette with the target electrode.
Align the device microports with target pMEA electrodes if using the multiport device.
If impedance measurement is available, turn on the patch clamp amplifier and initiate the impedance visualization software by clicking the 'Start' button.
Observe real-time impedance signals as the micropipette or device is lowered towards the retinal surface.
Lower the micropipette or device until it contacts the retinal surface, indicated by a rapid increase in impedance.
Save or make note of the position of the retinal surface upon contact.
If impedance measurement is unavailable, detect contact with the retinal surface through visual observation.
Lower the pipette or device until it visibly contacts the top surface of the Ames medium solution in the MEA chamber.
While observing the top of the retina with an inverted microscope, slowly lower the pipette or device until the top surface of the retina is visibly distorted.
Save or make note of the position for subsurface stimulation by lowering the pipette a further 40 μm (for S334ter-3 retinas) or 70 μm (for wild-type retinas).
Perform short duration (10 - 30 ms) injections using the pressure injection system at 0.1 psi to determine cell receptivity near the micropipette tip.
Observe neural signals with data acquisition software during pressure injection tests.
Orient the green LED toward the top surface of the retina.
Begin recording using the data acquisition software by typing the filename and clicking the "record" button.
Open the stimulus control program and load the default stimulus file by clicking the "Read Stimulus File" button.
Click on the "Run Stimulus File" button to initiate the default stimulus file consisting of 30 trials of 2 s ON and 2 s OFF full field flash at an intensity of 5 lm/m2 using the green LED.
Record 120 seconds of spontaneous activity without using the green LED.

Conduct 1 or more sets of glutamate injections, each set consisting of 30 trials with injection times ranging from 10 to 30 ms and pressures of 0.1 psi, approximately injecting 100 - 300 pL per trial.
Maintain an interpulse duration of 3 seconds between glutamate injections.
For multi-site injections, select 2 or more ports to inject simultaneously.
Record 90 seconds of spontaneous activity after the stimulus file has been completed.
Stop the recording by pressing the "Stop" button to save the file for future spike sorting and data analysis.
